sections.h2: What should I expect when selling a house in Woodbury?
sections.html:
Woodbury is one of the pricier east metro suburbs, and most sales here involve newer houses, active buyers and a short list of city rules about rentals and permits. The city is eight miles east of St. Paul along Interstate 94 in Washington County, and it is the seventh most populous city in Minnesota.

Because the houses are comparatively young, repair problems tend to be smaller than in older cities. The sellers who struggle are usually the ones with a tenant in place, an inherited house far from family, or a deadline that rules out a showing schedule.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show for Woodbury?
sections.html:
Woodbury had an estimated 81,558 residents on July 1, 2025, a gain of 8.6% over the April 2020 base of 75,105. It counted 61,961 people in 2010 and 46,463 in 2000, so the city has grown by about 75% since 2000.

  • 29,312 households averaging 2.66 people (2020 to 2024)
  • 77.6% of homes owner-occupied
  • Median owner-occupied home value: $450,200
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $2,412
  • Median gross rent: $1,908
  • Median household income: $125,310
  • 61.3% of adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree, and 5.3% of residents in poverty

High values mean a seller's equity is usually large, so the main question is speed and certainty rather than whether the sale clears the loan.

sections.h2: How did Woodbury grow from farmland to a suburb?
sections.html:
The area was first settled in 1844 and was originally called Red Rock before the name changed to honor Levi Woodbury, because another Red Rock Township already existed in Minnesota. It was mostly woods at first and then became farmland, and the township government was organized in 1858.

The first suburban development, Woodbury Heights, broke ground in 1955. Voters turned down a joint incorporation with Cottage Grove in 1963, 1,284 to 662, and then approved incorporating Woodbury alone on February 14, 1967, by 543 to 164. The village was officially incorporated on March 7, 1967. A 2025 estimate of 81,558 shows how far that decision carried it.

sections.h2: What does the land and neighborhood layout look like?
sections.html:
Woodbury covers 35.722 square miles, of which 34.895 are land. Interstate 94 forms the northern edge, 60th Street South the southern, Century Avenue the west and Manning Avenue the east. Neighbors include Oakdale, Lake Elmo, Cottage Grove, Maplewood, Newport and Afton.

The city sits on upland between the Mississippi and St. Croix river valleys. Small lakes dot it, including Powers, Wilmes, Colby and Carver, and the northeast corner drains to Valley Creek, one of the few remaining trout streams in the Twin Cities area. Woodbury maintains 63 parks covering about 3,600 acres and around 180 miles of mostly paved trails, which tends to be a selling point for houses near the lakes.

Climate data for the city show a January mean daily high of 23 degrees and a July high of 83, with about 32.6 inches of precipitation a year. Roofs, gutters and furnaces get tested every season.

sections.h2: What must a Woodbury landlord do before selling a rental house?
sections.html:
Any single family home, townhome or condominium rented in Woodbury needs a city rental license, and the license expires December 31 each year. There is no exemption for owners with only one rental unit. Exceptions exist for family-occupied homes, state-licensed nursing homes, some contract-for-deed sales while the buyer lives there, a fee waiver for owners on active military duty, and small state-licensed residential settings.

sections.h2: Are short-term rentals allowed in Woodbury?
sections.html:
No. City code prohibits renting a property for a term shorter than 30 days when the renter's permanent residence is elsewhere. That matters for a buyer who is pricing a house on vacation-rental income, and for a seller whose listing history shows nightly bookings.

Tell any serious buyer about past short-term use up front. The disclosure rules ask sellers to share material facts they know, and a code violation fits that description.

sections.h2: Which permits come up when you fix a Woodbury house for sale?
sections.html:
Woodbury uses a combination permit system. One permit covers building, plumbing, heating and cooling, and electrical fees for additions, basement finishes, decks, porches, remodels, repairs and new construction. Stand-alone flat-fee permits cover single replacements such as a furnace, air conditioner, water heater, water softener or EV charger outlet, and they go to the licensed contractor doing the work or to the homeowner.

  • Applications go through the city's online permitting portal
  • Residential contractors must hold a valid Minnesota license or a mechanical bond
  • Morning inspection windows run 9:30 to 11:30 a.m., so call by 9 a.m.
  • Afternoon windows run 1:30 to 3:30 p.m., so call by 1 p.m.

Call the Building Inspections Division at 651-714-3543 if you are unsure whether a project needs a permit. Finish and close any open permits before listing so a buyer's lender does not find them.

sections.h2: What taxes and recording steps apply at a Woodbury closing?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded with the Washington County Recorder. Minnesota's deed tax on a sale above $3,000 is .0033 of the net consideration under Minnesota Statutes 287.21, and it is due when the deed is presented for recording. At a $450,000 price, which is close to the city's median value, that works out to $1,485.

Your title company normally collects the tax and files the deed. Ask for the figure in the closing statement ahead of time, so you are not surprised on the day.

sections.h2: Who employs Woodbury residents, and how do they commute?
sections.html:
The city's 2022 financial report lists M Health Fairview with 1,013 employees, South Washington County Schools (District 833) with 964, Target with 864 and 3M with 759. Many residents also work at 3M's headquarters a few miles west in Maplewood. A large part of local business is retail, centered on Tamarack Village, Woodbury Village and Woodbury Lakes.

The mean commute is 23.9 minutes, and 98.0% of households have broadband. State Farm once employed about 2,000 people in a Woodbury building that opened in 1994; the company moved the work to Lincoln, Nebraska in 2006, and the vacant building was demolished in 2015 for redevelopment.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a rented house in Woodbury?
faqs.a: You need one to operate it as a rental until the sale closes. Single family homes, townhomes and condominiums rented in Woodbury all require a license, and the 2026 fee is $80 per unit.

faqs.q: Can a buyer run an Airbnb in Woodbury?
faqs.a: No. City code bans rentals under 30 days when the renter does not live there permanently.
Usually not. Owners complete a self-certification checklist each year, and the city inspects inside only for follow-up on a checklist item, an outstanding violation or a complaint.

faqs.q: How much is Minnesota deed tax on a Woodbury sale?
faqs.a: It is .0033 of the net consideration when the price is above $3,000, which is about $1,485 on a $450,000 sale. The tax is due when the deed is presented for recording.

faqs.q: Which county records a Woodbury deed?
faqs.a: Washington County. Contact its recorder's office for current filing fees, and confirm with your title company who will submit the paperwork.
